Answer all questions - no optional sections

questions.questionText: Imagine a busy road where buses move at a uniform speed and at regular intervals. As Reema moves along the road at a uniform speed, she notices that a bus comes from the opposite direction every 6 minutes, while another bus overtakes her from behind every 12 minutes. What is the regular time interval between a bus passing a stationary point on the road and the next bus in the same direction passing the same point?
In a quadratic equation, the sum of its roots is 9 less than their product. If one root exceeds the other by 3, what is the product of the roots?

Sunita runs a small dairy shop in her village. She usually sells premium-quality milk with 60% fat content at Rs 60 per liter. However, due to seasonal changes, the fat content in milk drops below 50%, and she reduced the selling price of milk by 25%. She purchases this pure milk from a local supplier at Rs 48 per liter. To ensure that her profit percentage remains the same even with the lower selling price, Sunita decides to add a certain amount of water to the milk before selling it. What percentage of water should Sunita mix with the pure milk to maintain her original profit percentage?

The prices of two commodities are in the ratio of 3:4. If the price of the first commodity is increased by p % and the price of the second commodity is decreased by 25%, then the new prices become in the ratio of 7:5. What is the value of p?

Ravi lends Rs 50,000 to two of his colleagues. He lends Rs 26,000 to the first colleague at a simple interest rate of 8% per annum. Ravi expects to earn 12% of the whole amount as profit. At what monthly compound interest rate does he lend the remaining amount to the second colleague?
Six years ago, a student was 1/6 times as old as his mentor. In six years, he will be 3/8 times the mentor’s age. What is the ratio of their current ages?

If the quadratic equation <inlineMath>{x^2} + 2px + q = 0</inlineMath> has two distinct real roots that differ by at most <inlineMath>2k</inlineMath>, then what is the possible range of values for <inlineMath>q</inlineMath>?

A car left City A at 10:00 am, heading towards City B at a speed of 72 km/h. Two hours later, another car started from City B towards City A at a speed of 90 km/h. Under normal conditions, the two cars were expected to meet at 2:30 pm. However, due to a roadblock that occurred at 1:00 pm, both cars had to reduce their speeds by the same amount, and as a result, they met at 5:30 pm instead. If the roadblock had occurred at 2:00 pm instead of 1:00 pm, at what time would the two cars have met?

A gym had a certain number of members enrolled in the year 2022. In 2023, the total number of members reduced by 20% compared to 2022. Out of the members in 2023, 80% were charged a membership fee that was 20% lower than the average fee in 2022, while the remaining 20% were charged 30% more than the average 2022 fee.
What was the absolute percentage change in the total membership fee collected by the gym in 2023 compared to 2022?

Mohan and Sohan are training for a mountain marathon in the hill town of Mussoorie. To improve their stamina, they first run on a flat 1260 m track, where Mohan beats Sohan by 420 m. A few days later, their coach challenges them to run on a sloping path. Mohan starts from the base of the slope, while Sohan starts from the top. They are asked to run towards each other, and they meet somewhere along the way. When they meet, Sohan has run 50 m more than Mohan. 
Compared to the normal speed, a runner's speed increases by 25% while going downhill and decreases by <inlineMath>28\frac{4}{7}\% </inlineMath>while running uphill. Find the total length of the sloping path.

Three numbers form an arithmetic sequence. The values that come from adding 1 to the first two numbers are prime numbers. The product of the largest number in the original series and these two primes equals 3094. Determine the sum of the three numbers in the sequence.
What is the sum of all two-digit numbers that give a remainder of 5 when they are divided by 9?

A water reservoir is being filled using 4 high-capacity pumps and 10 standard pumps. Each high-capacity pump can fill water twice as fast as each standard pump. All pumps are switched on at the same time when the reservoir is empty.
When the reservoir was expected to be full, due to an undetected crack at the base, the reservoir was found to be only two-thirds full. The crack was then partially sealed, reducing the leakage by 50%.
If all pumps working together (without any leakage) can fill the reservoir in 7.5 hours, how much additional time will it take to completely fill the reservoir after the leak was half sealed?

In a chocolate factory, there are four machines: A, B, C, and D.

  1. Machine A can produce a batch of chocolate bars in 8 hours.
  2. Machine B can produce a batch in 12 hours, but it requires maintenance for 1 hour after every 5 hours of operation.
  3. Machine C can produce a batch in 15 hours and can work continuously without breaks.
  4. Machine D can produce a batch in 10 hours and can work continuously without breaks.

Conditions:

  • Initially all machines start working together at the same time.
  • But after working for 3 hours Machine D suddenly breaks down and will require 2 hours for repairs. Then again starts working as usual.
  • After completing working for first 10 hours (including breaktime and repairing time) the machines work on alternate hours due to maintenance issue i.e

1st hr: Only A works

2nd hr: Only B works

3rd hr: Only C works

4th hr: only D works

This cycle continues until the production is completed. As machines work on alternate hours there is no extra breaktime need to be considered.  

How many batches are produced in the first 10 hours if there are a total of 20 batches? Determine the time required to complete the remaining batches.

(Do not round intermediate calculations, round final answers up to one decimal place if needed)

Consider a system with two interconnected tanks: Tank A and a swimming pool (Pool B). Tank A is filled with water through two inlet pipes (Pipe 1 and Pipe 2) and has one outlet pipe (Pipe 3) that transfers water to Pool B.
  • Pipe 1 can fill Tank A at a rate of 5 liters per minute.
  • Pipe 2 can fill Tank A at a rate of 3 liters per minute.
  • Pipe 3 can transfer water from Tank A to Pool B at a rate of 6 liters per minute.
Initially, Tank A is empty and it has a capacity of holding 160 liters. The following sequence occurs:
  1. Pipe 1 is opened and runs until Tank A and Pool B are completely filled.
  2. After 10 minutes, Pipe 2 is opened and runs until Tank A and Pool B are completely filled.
  3. After 5 minutes of opening pipe 2, Pipe 3 is opened to transfer water to Pool B while both Pipe 1 and Pipe 2 are still running.
Now determine the following:
  1. How much water is in Tank A after the first 15 minutes?
  2. How long will it take to fill Pool B if it has a capacity of 120 liters, starting from the moment Pipe 3 is opened?
  3. At what time will both Tank A and Pool B be filled to their respective capacities?

Seven authors, P, A, L, M, O, N and K, won the “Best Fiction Writer” award in different years between 2014 and 2020, with exactly one award being given each year and no author receiving the award more than once. Each author won for a different novel, and no novel was repeated.

The following information is known: 
  • L received the award for Whispers of Rain in a leap year.
  • A won the award just before K, for City of Dreams.
  • K received the award for Shadow Lines after L’s award.
  • Two authors received the award between A and P, who won it for Broken Truth.
  • P was not the last person to receive the award.
  • M received the award for Burning Skies in an odd-numbered year.
  • O was awarded for Silent Echoes before M, but O was not the first recipient.
  • N received the award for Midnight Notes.

In which of the following years, the award was given to novel ‘City of Dreams’?

To convert a number from octal to binary we need to convert octal to decimal first. Then the decimal part is converted to the binary part. Octal number is with base 8,decimal number is with base 10 and binary number is with base 2.
To convert octal to a decimal manually, you should first start multiplying the octal numbers by 8. Then, you raise it to a power of 0 and increase that power each time by 1 according to the octa decimal equivalent system. An example to convert octal to decimal is as follows:
<inlineMath>{123_8} = \left( {1 \times {8^2} + 2 \times {8^1} + 3 \times {8^0}} \right) = 64 + 16 + 3 = {83_{10}}</inlineMath>
To convert a decimal number to binary, Divide the decimal number by 2. Note the remainder (0 or 1). Divide the quotient obtained in the previous step by 2 again. Repeat previous steps 2 and 3 until the quotient is 0. Write the remainders in reverse order (from the last remainder to the first). This sequence of 0s and 1s is the binary equivalent of the decimal number. An example to convert octal to decimal is as follows:
<inlineMath>{83 \div 2 - Quotient - 41 - Remainder 1}</inlineMath>
<inlineMath>{41 \div 2 - Quotient - 20 - Remainder 1}</inlineMath>
<inlineMath>{20 \div 2 - Quotient - 10 - Remainder 0}</inlineMath>
<inlineMath>{10 \div 2 - Quotient - 5 - Remainder 0}</inlineMath>
<inlineMath>{5 \div 2 - Quotient - 2 - Remainder 1}</inlineMath>
<inlineMath>{2 \div 2 - Quotient - 1 - Remainder 0}</inlineMath>
<inlineMath>{1 \div 2 - Quotient - 0 - Remainder 1}</inlineMath>
Now the remainders in reverse order (from the last remainder to the first) is 1010011
<inlineMath>{83_{10}} = {1010011_2}</inlineMath>
Convert the octal number 7365₈ into its binary equivalent.

A restaurant has to prepare 600 identical dishes for a grand event. The work is assigned to four chefs: Chef A, Chef B, Chef C, and Chef D.
Their efficiencies under normal conditions are as follows:
  • Chef A can prepare all 600 dishes in 20 hours.
  • Chef B is 20% more efficient than Chef A.
  • Chef C is 40% less efficient than Chef A.
  • Chef D is a trainee and can prepare only one-third the number of dishes per hour as Chef B.
The working schedule and constraints are as follows:
  • All chefs start at 9:00 AM.
  • Chef A works continuously.
  • Chef B works continuously for the first 4 hours, then leaves.
  • Chef C works in shifts: 3 hours on, 1 hour off, repeating this cycle throughout.
  • Chef D joins 2 hours late but works continuously once he starts.
  • Due to a power outage, no work is done between 1:00 PM and 2:00 PM by any chef.
  • After 2:00 PM, Chef A’s efficiency drops by 10%, and Chef C’s efficiency increases by 25% due to better coordination.
At what time will all 600 dishes be completed?

Six participants are attending a week-long international conference held between “City A” and “City B.” Three of them are men and the rest are women. Two are attending for Research purposes, two for Collaboration, one for Presentation, and the remaining one for Observation. Two of them joined the conference in Bangkok, while one each joined in Cairo, Nairobi, Lisbon, and Helsinki. One participant is flying to Toronto, one to Paris, one to Dubai, and the rest to Berlin. Three of them are scientists, one is a doctor, one is a professor, and one is an architect.
  • Mr. Aarav Sen joined the conference in Nairobi. He is neither heading to Dubai nor to Paris. He is not attending for Collaboration or Presentation.
  • Dr. Dev Batra, a medical professional, joined at Lisbon. He is attending for Collaboration.
  • Miss Ananya Roy joined in Bangkok and is headed to Paris.
  • Mrs. Neha Desai also joined in Bangkok. She is attending for Collaboration and is flying to Berlin.
  • Mr. Kabir Nair is attending for Research and is flying to Berlin. He is an architect.
  • Miss Tara Kapoor is a professor based in Helsinki. She joined from there for Observation and is flying to Toronto.
Where is the scientist attending for Research headed to?

In 2023, several universities experienced significant fluctuations in scholarship distribution and student retention. As part of a broader analysis, it is crucial to calculate the total stipend disbursed to scholarship recipients, taking into account the impact of a mid-year dropout rate. The scholarships offered in each department varied, with students receiving stipends based on their eligibility. However, a portion of the scholarship recipients dropped out midway through the academic year, leading to a reduction in their stipend amounts. 
Data Set 1: University Admissions Data (2023)

Data Set 2: Scholarship Distribution and Stipend (2023)
Department % of Admitted Students Receiving Scholarship Average Annual Stipend per Scholarship Student (₹)
Engineering 30% 60,000
Management 25% 75,000
Law 40% 55,000
Humanities 35% 50,000
Sciences 45% 65,000

Assumptions:
  1. Scholarship Distribution: All scholarship students receive the full stipend amount for the full year unless they drop out mid-year.
  2. Dropout Rate: 10% of scholarship students in each department drop out mid-year. These students receive only half the stipend for the time they stayed at the university (6 months).
  3. Remaining Students: The remaining 90% of the scholarship students receive the full stipend for the full year.
In 2023, all scholarship students received the stipulated stipend amount. However, 10% of scholarship students in each department dropped out mid-year, and their stipend was reduced proportionally to the time spent at the university (assume they stayed for exactly 6 months). The rest received the full amount. 
Determine for which department the total allocated amount is the highest?
What is the total amount disbursed as stipend across all departments in 2023?

Seven athletes – A, B, C, D, E, F, and G – each participated in two different events: Sprint and Long Jump. Their performance scores in each event are unique and range from 1 to 7, such that no two athletes have the same score in any event.
  • Only E scored identically in both Sprint and Long Jump.
  • D's score in Sprint is 4 more than C's score in Sprint.
  • Only B and C have the same total score when both events are added.
  • The total score of D is exactly double that of G.
  • The Sprint score of B is equal to the Long Jump score of F.
  • The combined score of F across both events is 11.
  • At most two athletes have a lower Long Jump score than E.
  • Long Jump score of C is exactly double her Sprint score.

What is the difference between Sprint score of D and Long Jump score of G?

Six applicants — Aarav, Bhavna, Chirag, Divya, Esha, and Farooq — are being considered for a prestigious fellowship. Each candidate was evaluated on four fronts: academic score out of 100, fieldwork rating (Excellent, Good, Average, Poor), the number of environmental projects completed, and whether they had a disciplinary record. 
The rules are as follows: 
  1. To be eligible, a candidate must have an academic score of at least 75 and a fieldwork rating of at least “Good”.
  2. Any candidate with a disciplinary record is automatically disqualified, regardless of performance. 
  3. Candidates with more than 5 projects are exempted from the academic score condition, but not from the fieldwork rating. 
  4. If a candidate has fewer than 2 projects, they are eligible only if they scored above 85 and had a fieldwork rating of “Excellent”.
  5. Candidates with both academic scores above 90 and more than 3 projects are marked as Recommended. 
  6. Among the remaining eligible candidates, the top 2 with the highest number of projects are selected. 
  7. If two candidates tie in the number of projects, the one with the higher academic score gets preference. 
  8. Final selection includes all recommended candidates plus the top 2 from the rest. 
Candidate Details: 
  • Aarav scored 92, completed 4 projects, and was rated Good in fieldwork. No disciplinary record. 
  • Bhavna scored 88, completed 1 project, and received an Excellent rating. No disciplinary record. 
  • Chirag scored 80, completed 6 projects, fieldwork rating was Average, and had no record. 
  • Divya scored 76, completed 5 projects, fieldwork rated Excellent, no disciplinary issues. 
  • Esha scored 68, completed 7 projects, rated Good, but had a prior disciplinary warning. 
  • Farooq scored 91, completed 2 projects, rated Excellent, with a clean record.
Which of the candidates are selected?

An engineer is designing a solar panel array on a trapezoidal section of a factory roof. The trapezoid has:

Two parallel sides: 30 m and 50 m

Height between the parallel sides: 20 m

However, due to air vents and skylights, four identical circular openings (each of radius 2 m) must be left uncovered within the trapezoidal area.

A safety corridor, 2 m wide, must run along the entire boundary inside the trapezoid (like an inward border), where no panels can be placed.

What is the total area lost due to circular openings and safety corridor (the 2 m wide inward strip along all sides)?

If each panel covers 1.5 m² and costsRs.3,200, what is the total cost of installation?

The area A of a trapezoid is calculated using the formula:

<inlineMath>A = \frac{1}{2}({b_1} + {b_2}) \times h</inlineMath> 

Where <inlineMath>b{}_1</inlineMath> and <inlineMath>{b_2}</inlineMath> are the lengths of the two bases, and h is the height

Long ago, a group of five alchemists- Felix, Elise, Rowan, Arthur, and Paul discovered a hidden library containing lost texts on the 8 mystical substances and five labs in a row. These ancient scrolls described how to harness these materials to achieve true enlightenment—a state where one could wield magic, transform matter, and even achieve immortality. The mystical substances in the library are categorized into four types: Metals, Herbs, Crystal, and Elixirs. They are called "mystical" because alchemists throughout history believed these materials held magical or supernatural properties, capable of transforming matter, healing, and unlocking hidden knowledge.

The substances in each type are 

  • Metals – The Foundations of Transmutation: Gold and Silver 
  • Herbs – The Potions of Power: Mandrake and Nightshade
  • Crystals – The Stones of Power: Ruby and Sapphire
  • Elixirs – The Liquid Magic: Healing and Invisibility

To prove themselves as powerful, each alchemist had to choose exactly 3 mystical substances to study in their laboratory such that each of the 8 elements was in at least one of the labs. However, there were strict rules about which substances could be used together, based on their magical interactions. The rules in the scroll are

  1. Only one element is studied in 4 labs. 
  2. Silver is studied only in the two end labs and only the first lab has Gold.

  4. Felix's lab is in the middle and has exactly two kinds of herbs.
  5. No lab with healing elixir has herbs and no lab with invisibility elixir has Ruby.
  6. Elise's lab is not on either end of the row.
  7. Ruby must need Silver.
  8. Only Rowan has two kinds of metals.
  9. Elise studies neither herbs nor the healing elixir.
  10. Arthur has both Elixirs and the lab/labs only next to his has Nightshade.

Find the order of the labs.

options.text: Felix, Elise, Rowan, Arthur and Paul
Rowan, Elise, Felix, Arthur, and Paul
Rowan, Paul, Felix, Elise, and Arthur
Paul, Elise, Felix, Arthur, and Rowan

A steam power plant operates using water as the working fluid. The plant absorbs heat ⁠<inlineMath>{Q_{in}}⁠</inlineMath> from a high-temperature boiler, converting water into steam at a temperature of 300°C. The steam then drives a turbine, producing work W, before being condensed back into water in a condenser that operates at a temperature of 50 °C. If the plant has a thermal efficiency of 35%, calculate the amount of heat rejected ⁠<inlineMath>{Q_{out}}⁠</inlineMath> when the plant generates 500 kW of power over 5 hours.

Given that the specific heat capacity of water, c is ⁠<inlineMath>4.18\,kJ/kg^\circ C⁠</inlineMath> and the latent heat of vaporization, L is 2260 kJ/kg, determine the mass of water that is converted to steam during this time period.

The total work done over time is calculated as:

W=P×t

Where:

  • P = Power output (kW)
  • t = Time (hours)

The thermal efficiency (η) of the plant is given by:

⁠<inlineMath>\eta  = \frac{W}{{{Q_{in}}}}⁠</inlineMath>

Where:

  • W = Work output (kJ)
  • Qin = Heat input (kJ)

The heat rejected (Qout) can be calculated using:

Qout=Qin−W

 

Qin​ = Heat input (kJ) 

W = Work output (kJ)

The total heat used for converting water to steam can be expressed as:

Qin=m⋅L

Where:

m = Mass of water converted to steam (kg)

L = Latent heat of vaporization (kJ/kg)

Factor of conversion: 1 kW = 1 kJ/s=3600 kJ/hr

  • On the second day, he sells 1/4th of what was left at a 60% profit.
  • On the third day, he sells 25% of what was left at a 30% profit.
  • On the fourth day, he sells 60 tomatoes at no profit, no loss.

  • On the sixth day, he throws 50 tomatoes and sells 50% of what was left at a 35% loss.

Banking methods play a crucial role in shaping the health and direction of a nation’s economy. Traditional banking focuses primarily on savings, loans, and basic financial services, fostering trust and stability in the financial system. However, the rise of modern banking methods such as digital banking, mobile wallets, and algorithm-driven lending has transformed how people and businesses interact with money.

With increased access to credit and faster transaction processing, modern banking has accelerated economic activities by encouraging consumption, investment, and entrepreneurship. Small businesses now rely on quick online loans, while individuals benefit from real-time fund transfers and financial management tools. On the other hand, this rapid digitisation has also introduced new economic vulnerabilities, such as cybersecurity risks and financial exclusion of those unfamiliar with technology.

Thus, while evolving banking methods have stimulated economic growth, they also demand stronger regulation and greater financial literacy to ensure inclusive and stable development.

Based on the passage, which of the following is the most accurate cause and effect relationship being discussed?

options.text: Traditional banking systems caused financial exclusion and mistrust, leading to a rise in digital banking.
The shift to modern banking methods has expanded economic opportunities, but it has also created new financial challenges.
Modern banking systems replaced traditional ones to promote only technological advancement, not economic growth.
Increased digital banking caused a decline in individual savings, leading to long-term economic instability.

questions.questionText:
Once battling unregulated waste disposal, open dumping grounds, and indifferent public participation, Indore—now repeatedly ranked as India’s cleanest city has undergone a profound transformation that extends far beyond cosmetic sanitation drives. This metamorphosis is rooted in a blend of administrative innovation, decentralised waste governance, and most importantly, a cultural reorientation of its citizens.
The city introduced a meticulous system of waste segregation at source, real-time GPS tracking of collection vehicles, and extensive use of mobile applications for citizen grievances. However, technology alone did not drive the change. The Indore Municipal Corporation worked in collaboration with NGOs, local influencers, and neighbourhood committees to conduct awareness campaigns that reframed cleanliness as a collective duty rather than a top-down mandate.
The city invested in transforming its most neglected urban spaces, slums and landfill zones, into centres of hygiene advocacy. Community-led cleanliness pledges, door-to-door waste education, and even reward mechanisms for compliant households became standard. Over time, public behaviour shifted from apathy to ownership, embedding cleanliness into the city's identity.
Indore’s success is not just a testament to effective urban planning or policy execution, but a case study in behavioural change, decentralised governance, and the power of consistent civic engagement. The city’s approach signals a broader lesson: enduring cleanliness cannot be imposed; it must be cultivated from within.
Which of the following best summarises the central message of the passage?

options.text: While technology and strict municipal regulations play an important role in ensuring cleanliness, Indore’s transformation primarily highlights how embedding civic values and shared responsibility within communities can lead to sustainable urban development.

The case of Indore reveals that urban cleanliness can be achieved through a top-down strategy that focuses on slum redevelopment, relocation of dumping grounds, and a systematic reliance on public–private infrastructure funding.

Indore’s success in sanitation is driven by its prioritisation of technological innovation and regulatory reforms, supported by a cooperative government model that centralises control and reduces dependence on public engagement.

The transformation of Indore into India’s cleanest city exemplifies how intensive monitoring systems and rigorous enforcement mechanisms, when paired with high municipal investment, form the cornerstone of urban hygiene reform.

questions.questionText:
Sustainable farming plays a critical role in protecting the environment while ensuring long-term food security. Unlike conventional agricultural methods that often rely on chemical fertilizers, monoculture, and excessive water usage, sustainable farming practices aim to preserve natural resources, enhance soil health, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. By using techniques such as crop rotation, organic fertilization, integrated pest management, and conservation tillage, sustainable agriculture minimises environmental degradation and fosters biodiversity.

It also enhances carbon sequestration through practices like agroforestry and cover cropping, contributing to climate change mitigation. Importantly, it empowers local communities by promoting resilience and self-sufficiency, especially in regions vulnerable to climate variability. As the global population grows and environmental challenges intensify, transitioning to sustainable farming is no longer a choice; it is a necessity for a healthier planet and a more secure future.

Which of the following best describes a cause-and-effect relationship from the passage?

options.text: The use of genetically modified crops causes farmers to earn higher profits.
Chemical fertilizers cause soil to become permanently fertile, ensuring food security.
Adopting sustainable farming practices leads to improved soil health and reduced environmental harm.
Excessive water usage causes sustainable farming to become the dominant agricultural method

questions.questionText:
Myths have long served as vessels of collective imagination, carrying the beliefs, values, and fears of ancient cultures. In modern literature, these age-old stories are often reimagined to explore contemporary issues such as identity, gender, power, and morality. Authors use mythological frameworks not just to retell old tales, but to question or subvert them. Retellings of Greek myths might highlight the silenced voices of female characters or reinterpret heroic narratives from alternative viewpoints. These adaptations allow writers to connect the ancient and the modern, offering a deeper reflection on today’s society.
The resurgence of myths in modern storytelling has caused a significant shift in how readers engage with literature. Familiar mythic structures lend emotional resonance and symbolic depth to new works, while the reinterpretation of known characters encourages readers to reconsider their assumptions. This blending of the old and the new has also sparked greater interest in classical literature, allowing myths to serve as cultural bridges across time. 
Which of the following best illustrates the cause-and-effect relationship discussed in the passage about myths in modern literature?

options.text: The reinterpretation of myths in modern texts disrupts traditional narratives and fosters critical engagement with present-day social structures.
Modern literature uses myths primarily as decorative elements to enhance aesthetic appeal.
The historical accuracy of ancient myths limits their relevance in modern literary forms.
The popularity of modern literature has rendered ancient myths obsolete and disconnected from contemporary discourse.

questions.questionText:
The BIS (Bureau of Indian Standards) Mark is a certification mark utilised in India to indicate that a product conforms to the national safety standards set by the BIS, the countrywide requirements framework. This mark is particularly important for customer items including electrical home equipment, packaged food, and cement, in which safety and reliability are vital. When a product bears the BIS Mark, it assures customers that the product has passed rigorous testing and meets requirements associated with performance, durability, and protection.

The BIS Mark helps prevent the sale of substandard or fake products, builds consumer trust, and protects public health. It also encourages manufacturers to meet quality standards, promoting fair competition in the market. In many cases, BIS certification is mandatory before products can be sold in India. Through the BIS Mark, the government ensures high product quality.

Which statement best summarises the passage?

options.text: The BIS Mark is a symbol of national pride and has been in use since India's independence.
The BIS Mark is a certification that guarantees a product is environmentally friendly and recyclable.
The BIS Mark assures the quality and safety of products, protects consumers, and promotes fair competition among manufacturers.
The BIS Mark is optional for most products and serves mainly as a decorative label for branding.

questions.questionText:
Leadership styles refer to the different ways leaders guide, motivate, and manage teams. Common styles include authoritarian, democratic, and laissez-faire leadership. Authoritarian leaders tend to make decisions independently and expect strict compliance, which can lead to efficiency but may suppress creativity. Democratic leaders, on the other hand, encourage participation and value team input, often resulting in higher morale and more innovative outcomes. 

Laissez-faire leaders provide minimal supervision, trusting team members to make their own decisions—a method that can empower skilled teams but may cause confusion in less experienced groups. Effective leaders often adapt their style depending on the context, team dynamics, and organisational goals. Rather than strictly adhering to one method, successful leadership frequently involves a balance of firmness, collaboration, and flexibility to achieve results.

What can be inferred about the relationship between leadership flexibility and organisational success?

options.text: A leader's primary role is to define strict procedures that minimise variability, regardless of team composition or task.
The most effective leadership style is one that minimises team autonomy to ensure accountability and uniformity.
Success in leadership is contingent upon the leader's ability to evaluate situational variables and selectively apply characteristics from multiple leadership styles.
Consistent use of democratic leadership ensures success because it encourages participation and automatically leads to innovation.

questions.questionText:
The popularity of self-driving cars hinges not only on technological advancement but also on public trust and practical benefits. For people to adopt autonomous vehicles widely, they must feel confident in their safety and reliability. Features such as real-time obstacle detection, adaptive learning algorithms, and fail-safe emergency controls are crucial in establishing this trust. 

Beyond safety, convenience and personalisation play major roles. Self-driving cars that offer smart route planning, voice-controlled interfaces, and seamless integration with smartphones and digital assistants can appeal to tech-savvy users. Accessibility features for the elderly and people with disabilities, along with eco-friendly designs like electric powertrains, can broaden the vehicle’s appeal to wider demographics.

Which of the following best captures the complex interplay of factors influencing the future acceptance of self-driving cars as implied by the passage?

options.text: Without emotional appeal and social inclusivity, even the most advanced autonomous technologies may struggle to gain public trust and widespread adoption.
Widespread acceptance of self-driving cars is inevitable due to rapid advancements in artificial intelligence and machine learning.
The environmental advantages of self-driving cars will override public concern about safety and personal autonomy.
Self-driving cars will primarily succeed by eliminating the need of human intervention in all transportation scenarios.

questions.questionText:
Passage:

Nelson Mandela played a pivotal role in the fight against Apartheid in South Africa, emerging as a global symbol of resistance to racial injustice. Apartheid was a system of institutionalised racial segregation and discrimination enforced by the white minority government from 1948 to 1994. Mandela, a member of the African National Congress (ANC), initially advocated non-violent resistance but later co-founded the ANC’s armed wing, Umkhonto we Sizwe, in response to the brutal suppression of peaceful protests. 

Arrested in 1962, Mandela spent 27 years in prison, becoming a symbol of hope and defiance for millions. Despite the harsh conditions, he remained steadfast in his vision for a democratic and inclusive South Africa. His release in 1990 marked a turning point, as he led negotiations with the apartheid regime to dismantle the system peacefully. In 1994, Mandela became the country’s first Black president, ushering in a new era of reconciliation and nation-building. 

What was a major effect of Nelson Mandela's imprisonment for 27 years during the apartheid era in South Africa?

options.text: It caused the collapse of the Apartheid government immediately.
It led to increased international support for his cause, and pressure to end Apartheid.
It resulted in Mandela abandoning the fight against racial injustice.
It strengthened Apartheid laws across South Africa.

questions.questionText:
Buddha Purnima, also referred to as Vesak, holds profound spiritual and cultural significance for Buddhists around the world. It commemorates the delivery, enlightenment, and demise (Maha Parinirvana) of Gautama Buddha, all of which might be believed to have happened on the full moon day. This sacred occasion is marked by reflection on the Buddha's teachings of compassion, mindfulness, and the route to liberation from suffering.

At present, devotees go to temples, offer prayers, meditate, and engage in acts of generosity which include feeding the poor or freeing captive animals, symbolising kindness and admiration for all life. The teachings of Buddha, particularly the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path, encourage humans to lead ethical, peaceful lives rooted in inner focus. The celebration of Buddha Purnima encourages not only private, spiritual growth, but also  harmony and non-violence in society.

Which of the following best explains the cause-and-effect relationship highlighted in the passage?

options.text: As people want to celebrate a holiday, temples are decorated and processions are organised.
Since Buddha's life events occurred on the same day, Buddha Purnima is considered deeply sacred and symbolic.
As the day is culturally significant, people ignore the core teachings of Buddha and focus on rituals.
As people engage in acts of devotion, they are expected to gain material rewards and blessings.

questions.questionText:
Indian educational strategies have traditionally focused on memorization, disciplined practice, and a deep respect for teachers. Influenced by ancient systems like the Gurukul, the education system emphasizes theoretical knowledge and standardized testing. While this approach helps build a strong academic foundation, it often restricts opportunities for open discussion, critical thinking, and creativity in the classroom.

In contrast, British educational techniques prioritise analytical thinking, interactive learning, and unbiased inquiry. British classrooms regularly encourage students to challenge assumptions, take part in discussions, and broaden unique thoughts via essays and initiatives. Assessment within the British system generally values knowledge and articulation over memorisation.

Though each structure has evolved over the years, Indian techniques generally tend to take cognisance more of examination overall performance and factual accuracy, while British strategies intend to develop argumentation abilities and intellectual independence. As global schooling moves toward interdisciplinary and learner-focused methods, each system faces the challenge of integrating traditional strengths with current academic demands.

Which of the following best captures a deeper implication of the comparison made in the passage?

options.text: Indian academic techniques are outdated and should be entirely replaced by British techniques.
The British education system is superior because it avoids standardised testing and memorisation.
Both systems reflect their cultural values and offer unique strengths, but must evolve to meet the needs of modern education.
Indian education has no room for creativity and should not be considered effective.

questions.questionText:
Personal identity refers to the concept of what makes an individual the same person over time despite various physical, psychological, and situational changes. It explores the core elements that define a person's unique characteristics, memories, values, and experiences. Philosophers have long debated whether personal identity is rooted in the continuity of consciousness, memory, bodily persistence, or social recognition. Some argue that memory plays a central role, suggesting that our ability to recall past experiences helps establish a sense of self. 

Others emphasise the importance of bodily continuity or the consistent traits and moral values that shape one's personality. In modern discourse, identity is also influenced by culture, relationships, and personal choices. The evolving nature of identity raises important questions about authenticity, self-perception, and the influence of society in shaping who we are.

Given the multidimensional perspectives on personal identity presented in the passage, which of the following best reflects the philosophical tension underlying its construction?

options.text: The belief that identity is solely a product of individual memory denies the role of body and social influence.
The assertion that personality traits remain unchanged suggests that identity is entirely predetermined at birth.
The tension between internal continuity and external recognition highlights identity as a construct negotiated between self-perception and societal interpretation.
The idea that bodily persistence guarantees identity implies a universal, culture-free model of selfhood.

questions.questionText:

questions.questionText:
Democratic governance is often praised for its ability to ensure citizen participation, uphold individual rights and maintain governmental accountability. Supporters argue that democratic systems create a more just society by allowing free elections, protecting civil liberties and preventing authoritarian rule. They believe that public involvement in decision-making leads to fairer policies that reflect the will of the people. Critics, however, contend that democracy can be inefficient, leading to political gridlock, slow decision-making and susceptibility to populism. They argue that in times of crisis, decisive leadership is often hindered by the complexities of democratic debate and bureaucracy.
Which of the following arguments supports the importance of democratic governance?

options.text: Political gridlock and slow decision-making hinder progress in democratic systems.
Free elections and civil liberties ensure a just and accountable government.
Democratic systems are prone to populism and instability.
In times of crisis, authoritarian rule allows for more decisive leadership.

questions.questionText:
From primitive stone tools to advanced autonomous drones, the evolution of warfare reflects humanity's relentless pursuit of dominance and security. In ancient times, tribal conflicts were resolved with rudimentary weapons made of bone or wood. With the rise of civilizations came organized armies, chariots, and the introduction of metallurgy, which revolutionized weapon-making. 
The Middle Ages witnessed the prominence of fortresses, cavalry, and siege warfare, while the invention of gunpowder transformed battlefields in the early modern era. In the 20th century, two world wars ushered in mechanized and nuclear warfare, profoundly altering geopolitical balances. Today, cyber capabilities and artificial intelligence hint at a future where war may be waged without traditional battlegrounds. The trajectory of warfare mirrors both technological advancement and the enduring complexities of human conflict.
After reading the passage, select the correct tone of the same.

The economic system of any country is broadly divided into 3 main sectors: the primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors, each playing a crucial function in the functioning of the economy. The number one sector entails activities that make use of natural resources, including agriculture, mining, forestry, and fishing. This sector is the inspiration of an economy, because it produces raw materials for processing. The secondary sector makes a speciality of production, reworking raw materials into completed merchandise. It is pushed via industries such as textiles, car, electronics, and chemicals, and frequently acts as the backbone of industrialisation and urbanisation.

The tertiary sector, also known as the service sector, includes industries like retail, hospitality, healthcare, schooling, information technology, and finance. Over the years, this area has seen first-rate growth, specifically in advanced economies, driven by technological improvements and changing customer demands. In emerging economies like India, the growth of the service sector has become increasingly important, as it contributes significantly to both GDP and employment.

Which of the following best summarises the passage on the sectors of the economy?

options.text: The primary sector remains the most significant in any economy due to its dominance in global markets, while the secondary and tertiary sectors have seen marginal growth due to the ongoing technological revolution.

Economic development is characterised by the shift from reliance on the primary sector to growth in the secondary and tertiary sectors, with a critical balance necessary for sustainable economic stability.

The tertiary sector’s explosive growth in emerging economies like India has been largely driven by the expansion of industrial production in the primary and secondary sectors, which has diminished the role of services in global GDP.

While the primary sector is essential for raw material extraction, the secondary and tertiary sectors have stagnated in recent years, leading to a diminishing role of industry and services in economic development.

George Orwell’s 1984 is an effective exploration of a dystopia in which a totalitarian regime controls every aspect of existence—even thoughts. Orwell, driven by his studies of oppressive political structures, crafted a situation in which ‘Big Brother’ watches over residents continuously, implementing conformity and punishing individuality. The novel serves best as a warning about authoritarianism, and additionally, as a mirror image of human resilience and the iconic preference for freedom. Through Winston Smith, the protagonist who dares to revolt in opposition to the machine, Orwell reveals the mental toll of residing under steady surveillance and manipulation. Despite Winston’s defeat, the radical book leaves readers wondering whether genuine freedom lies in physical escape or the strength of an independent notion.

Based on the passage, what deeper message is Orwell conveying through 1984?

options.text: Totalitarianism is an effective way to maintain social order.
Even in the face of oppression, the human spirit’s longing for freedom persists.
Surveillance and control are necessary for a stable society.
Rebellion against authority is always successful in the end.

questions.questionText:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), as the country's central bank, performs a pivotal function not only in regulating the monetary framework, but also in shaping the country’s monetary stability. During times of inflation, the RBI employs tools including increasing the repo rate to reduce cash available, thereby discouraging excessive borrowing and spending. Conversely, in instances of economic slowdown, it lowers interest rates to stimulate growth. 

However, the effects of such interventions aren't always immediate or predictable. For instance, an unexpected hike in the repo rate might manage inflation but can concurrently stifle personal funding and consumer confidence. 

Additionally, RBI’s regulatory oversight on banks, digital transactions, and foreign exchange reserves ensures systemic confidence. Its evolving virtual initiatives and policy shifts significantly have an effect on public behaviour and market sentiment, reinforcing its role as more than just a financial authority; it acts as a stabilising force in instances of financial uncertainty.

Based on the passage, which of the following is the most accurate cause-and-effect relationship being discussed?

options.text: The RBI's shift to digital governance directly results in immediate inflationary control.
Strategic manipulation of repo rates by the RBI may temper inflation, but can inadvertently suppress entrepreneurial borrowing.
The RBI's regulation of foreign exchange reserves is the sole determinant of public market sentiment.
Economic slowdown causes RBI to tighten monetary policy to prevent reckless public expenditure.

questions.questionText:
The internet has revolutionised how the younger era learns, communicates, and perceives. While it gives instantaneous access to data and international connectivity, it also subtly shapes intellectual and emotional improvement. Prolonged screen time, social media comparisons, and the steady pressure to remain visible online have brought about growing ranges of anxiety, reduced attention spans, and identity issues among teenagers. 

At the same time, the net empowers self-expression and mastering opportunities, making it a double-edged sword. The psychological results are often complex, supplying both empowerment and emotional vulnerability depending on how the internet is used.

What can be inferred about the psychological impact of the internet on youth based on the passage?

options.text: The internet’s role in youth development is contradictory, promoting growth while potentially destabilising emotional well-being.
The internet’s cognitive benefits significantly outweigh its emotional consequences for young users.
Psychological issues in youth are more influenced by parental control than by online behaviour.
Limiting access to the internet is the most effective way to ensure stable emotional development in adolescents.

questions.questionText:
The Great Depression of the 1930s was more than a collapse of markets; it dismantled the psychological scaffolding upon which millions built their identities and aspirations. As unemployment surged and economic institutions crumbled, people confronted not just the absence of income but the erosion of hope, autonomy, and purpose. Traditional social roles, especially for men, who were often the primary earners, were upended, causing widespread feelings of inadequacy and shame. Families, once stable units of mutual support, became sites of tension and despair, with children forced to mature quickly and forgo education or dreams. 

The psychological toll extended beyond the immediate generation: survivors often developed risk-averse mindsets, hyper-frugality, and emotional detachment, traits passed down through parenting styles and social norms. This emotional inheritance shaped how entire communities responded to future crises cautiously, anxiously, and with deep mistrust of economic systems. In this way, the Great Depression functioned as a generational trauma, embedding itself not only in policy and memory but in personality and culture.

Which of the following best reflects the complex cause-and-effect dynamic described in the passage, especially regarding the intergenerational psychological legacy of the Great Depression?

options.text: The immediate economic hardship caused individuals to adapt with optimism and resilience, traits that helped buffer long-term emotional damage.
The collapse of financial systems led directly to policy reform but had little influence on personal identity or family dynamics.
Widespread economic instability fractured personal identities and family roles, leading to long-term emotional coping patterns that shaped future generations’ behaviours and worldviews.
Feelings of shame and fear during the Great Depression were primarily caused by lack of access to modern psychological support services, which could have prevented long-term trauma.

questions.questionText:
The Ganga River, also known as the Ganges, is one of the most sacred and significant rivers in India. Originating from the Gangotri Glacier in the Himalayas, it flows through northern India and Bangladesh before emptying into the Bay of Bengal. The river supports the livelihoods of millions of people by providing water for agriculture, industry, and domestic use. However, over the years, excessive pollution from industrial waste, sewage, and religious offerings has severely affected its water quality. As a result, efforts like the ‘Namami Gange’ mission have been launched to clean and conserve the river.

What is the most accurate cause-and-effect relationship described in the passage?

options.text: The Ganga flows through northern India because it is sacred.
The Ganga supports agriculture because it is a long river.
Pollution has increased due to growing population and industrial activities
The Namami Gange mission was launched to promote tourism.
